headline: ECE Educator-Scholar | Intelligent Sensing, Signal Processing & Wireless AI
tagline: Undergraduate Teaching & Mentoring | Hands-On ECE Labs | Applied AI Research
summary: PhD in Electrical and Computer Engineering (University of Oklahoma, 2025) with experience teaching undergraduate engineering, supervising labs, mentoring student projects, and conducting applied research. Scholarship connects wireless AI, reproducible experimental platforms, and wearable sensing for health monitoring. Interested in project-based ECE teaching, interdisciplinary sensing systems, and research that actively involves undergraduate students.
researchInterests: Wireless AI and Networked Cyber-Physical Systems
dissertationFocus: PhD dissertation focused on AI/ML for wireless networks, including data-efficient radio propagation modeling, generative augmentation, robust learning under distribution shift, network self-healing, and reproducible simulation and experimental evaluation.

skills.Teaching & Undergraduate Research: Undergraduate engineering instruction, laboratory facilitation, project and thesis mentoring, applied programming, hands-on experimentation, curriculum alignment, and student-centered technical feedback
skills.Sensing, Signals & Intelligent Systems: Smartwatch inertial sensing, time-series analysis, activity recognition, digital signal processing, sensor data collection, wearable health monitoring, cyber-physical data analysis
skills.Experimental ECE & Communications: 3GPP-informed wireless simulation, cellular communication systems, 5G testbed design, network measurements, model-based evaluation, experimental design, and digital twins
skills.Machine Learning & Control-Oriented AI: Deep learning, generative augmentation, transfer and domain-adaptive learning, reinforcement learning, network self-healing and adaptive optimization
skills.Software & Research Platforms: Python, C/C++, PyTorch, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, Pandas, NumPy, SQL, Linux, and Git

Supported departmental workshops, student orientations, and laboratory learning activities.
mentoringBullets: Mentored undergraduate and graduate students in wireless ML experiments and research writing.
